description: The core cross-field rule (CONSTRAINT_INVALIDATES_PASS): a result CANNOT have both passed=true and a constraint_violations entry with invalidates_result=true -- that combination is the exact failure mode this field exists to prevent (a consumer trusting `passed` alone would count a disqualified result as a success). This is a hand-rolled-only check, the same class of cross-field rule as SELF_PARENT (Discussion #45) and DUPLICATE_ATTEMPT (Discussion #22): the raw JSON Schema's properties/required vocabulary can't express "if any array item has invalidates_result=true then a sibling top-level field must equal false" without a $data reference, so this fixture's `expect.valid: false` only holds against the hand-rolled validators (validate_result_set / validateResultSet), not the schema alone -- see sdk/python/tests/test_schema_consistency.py's mirrored test for the explicit documentation of that gap.
